title: Shifting the Inverse-Square Graph Left and Down
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The graph of y = 1 / x^2 is to be shifted left 2 units and down 1 unit. Give an equation for the shifted graph and describe its asymptotes and intercepts.

steps.title: Apply the Horizontal Shift (Left 2 Units)
steps.explanation: Replace x with x + 2 in y = 1/x^2 to shift the graph 2 units to the left.
steps.why: Replacing x with x + 2 moves the vertical asymptote from x = 0 to x = -2.

steps.title: Apply the Vertical Shift (Down 1 Unit)
steps.explanation: Subtract 1 from the right-hand side (or replace y with y + 1) to shift the graph 1 unit downward.
steps.why: Subtracting 1 moves the horizontal asymptote from y = 0 to y = -1.

steps.title: Identify the Shifted Asymptotes and Intercepts
steps.explanation: Setting y = 0 gives (x + 2)^2 = 1, so x = -3 and x = -1 are the x-intercepts. Setting x = 0 gives y = 1/4 - 1 = -3/4 as the y-intercept.
steps.why: Solving y = 0 and evaluating y(0) locates the exact axis crossings of the translated curve.
